title: Golden CI: parallelize two-replay tests to reduce sequential wait
description:
The 3 two-replay tests (mana_drain_fact_or_fiction, savannah_lions_trade, stack_resolved) run sequentially and take ~260s combined:

- mana_drain_fact_or_fiction: ~116-128s
- savannah_lions_trade: ~74-85s
- stack_resolved: ~74-76s

These tests spawn their own subprocess clients and don't share state with the persistent bridge/potato fixtures. They could potentially run in parallel using:
- Separate XMage server instances on different ports
- Separate tables on the same server (if usernames don't collide)
- pytest-xdist with careful fixture isolation

The main constraint is that they currently run first (before persistent fixtures) to avoid username collisions. Parallelizing would require unique usernames per test or separate servers.

Expected savings: ~100-150s (~1.5-2 min) if all 3 run concurrently (limited by the slowest, ~128s).
